mud-pump.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (reciprocating pump) / API 7K mud system
mud-pump.drawn: Reciprocating pump symbol (circle with a piston and crank) on the mud system flow sheet, with a pulsation dampener (small dome) on the discharge going to the standpipe manifold and suction from the mud tanks; usually two or three pumps in parallel.
mud-pump.notes: The dampener dome and the mud / standpipe service distinguish it from a process plunger pump (reciprocating-pump). Only on drilling flow sheets.

choke-manifold.standard: API 16C / API RP 53 well-control schematic, ISO 10628-2 valves
choke-manifold.drawn: From the BOP choke line: two gate valves into a cross or header, then parallel branches each with a gate valve and a choke (bow-tie with a diagonal arrow), rejoining to the mud-gas separator or flare; a straight-through bleed line in the middle on many manifolds.
choke-manifold.notes: Production chokes on a tree are single valves; a choke manifold has several parallel choke branches with block valves. Only on well-control schematics.

shale-shaker.standard: Drilling mud system flow sheet convention (API RP 13C)
shale-shaker.drawn: A box with a sloping dashed screen deck: returns from the flowline enter one end, cuttings leave off the low end of the screen, and the cleaned mud drops through to the tank below; vibrator motors drawn on the basket.
shale-shaker.notes: Dashed sloping screen = shaker. Desanders and desilters on the mud system are cyclones (cones); a degasser is a vessel.

mud-tank.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (open tank with agitators) / API RP 13C mud system
mud-tank.drawn: An open-topped rectangular tank divided into compartments, each with an agitator (motor M on a shaft with impeller blades) and the mud level dashed; suction to the mud pumps and returns from the shakers.
mud-tank.notes: Open top plus agitators = mud pit. A closed process vessel is drawn as a capsule. Pit volume totaliser (PVT) level transmitters sit on each compartment. ISA codes here: LT = pit volume.

plet.standard: Subsea field layout / subsea P&ID convention (API 17P)
plet.drawn: On subsea P&IDs: the pipeline ending at a structure (dashed boundary) with an isolation valve and a connection hub (clamp or collet connector, drawn as a pair of thick bars or a hub outline) for the spool or jumper; on field layouts a small rectangle at the pipeline end.
plet.notes: A PLEM is the same idea with several hubs or a manifold header. Topsides pig traps and risers are separate items.

subsea-manifold.drawn: Subsea P&ID: a dashed structure boundary containing production and test headers with each well slot (jumper hub) branching to both headers through its own subsea valves, and header outlets to the flowlines; on field layouts a rectangle with the wells radiating to it.
subsea-manifold.notes: Same branching logic as a topsides production-manifold, but inside a subsea structure boundary with hubs instead of flanges. A single-hub structure at a pipeline end is a PLET.

umbilical-termination-assembly.standard: Subsea control system schematic / field layout convention (API 17E)
umbilical-termination-assembly.drawn: On subsea control schematics: the umbilical (a thick double line or bundle) ending at a termination head inside a dashed structure, fanning out to hydraulic, chemical and electrical couplers that connect by flying leads to trees and manifolds.
umbilical-termination-assembly.notes: A structure where the umbilical bundle splits into many small hydraulic / electrical lines is a UTA or SUTU; one carrying production pipework is a manifold or PLET.

subsea-tree.standard: API 17D subsea P&ID convention, drawn like the surface tree (ISO 10628-2 valves)
subsea-tree.drawn: Same valve stack as a surface tree, but every valve is actuated (small actuator boxes), it sits inside a dashed subsea boundary above the seabed line, and an annulus line and SCSSV control line run alongside. Production master (PMV), production wing (PWV) and the subsea choke sit on the side outlet to the flowline or jumper.
subsea-tree.notes: A dashed subsea boundary, seabed line and all-actuated valves distinguish it from a surface christmas-tree. PMV / PWV / AMV / AWV are subsea valve tags, not ISA letter codes.

pipe-handling-catwalk.standard: Layout plan convention (drill floor / pipe deck layout)
pipe-handling-catwalk.drawn: Drill-floor and pipe-deck layouts: a long rectangle with the trough centreline aimed at the V-door, pipe racks drawn as parallel lines along both sides, and an arrow towards the drill floor.
pipe-handling-catwalk.notes: Only on drilling layouts, never on P&IDs.

cement-unit.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary; reciprocating pumps)
cement-unit.drawn: On well-service schematics: a dash-dot skid boundary with displacement / mixing tanks and two reciprocating (triplex) pump symbols discharging into a common high-pressure line to the cement head or standpipe.
cement-unit.notes: Twin reciprocating pumps on a skid with displacement tanks = cement unit; a single mud pump with a dampener is a mud-pump. Usually on temporary well-service layouts rather than process P&IDs.

datasheet.form: Cementing unit datasheet (API 7K pumps, DNV 2.7-3 skid)

coiled-tubing-unit.drawn: Well-intervention layouts: a reel (two concentric circles) with the tubing running over the gooseneck to the injector head (box) above the well-control stack on the well; the control cabin and power pack are rectangles beside the reel.
coiled-tubing-unit.notes: Temporary equipment, not shown on process P&IDs. The stack below the injector is a well-control item (bop-stack).

datasheet.form: Coiled tubing equipment datasheet (API RP 16ST, API 5ST tubing)

transformer.drawn: Two overlapping circles (one per winding) on the single-line diagram, with the HV feeder above and the LV feeder below. Winding symbols (Δ, Y, Yn) and the MVA / kV rating are written beside it; a diagonal arrow through both circles marks an on-load tap changer.
transformer.notes: Two circles = two-winding transformer; three circles = three-winding. ANSI drawings show two facing coils instead. Two circles in a P&ID instrument context are not used, so this symbol is almost always electrical.

switchgear.drawn: Thick horizontal busbar with an incoming feeder and several outgoing feeders, each through a circuit breaker (a switch blade with a small × on the fixed contact) or contactor, often inside a dashed boundary with the board tag and voltage.
switchgear.notes: Breaker: × on the contact. Disconnector: a bar across the contact. Contactor (MCC starter): a half-circle on the contact. On layouts a switchgear line-up is a long rectangle divided into panels inside an E-house.

e-house.standard: Layout plan convention (plot plan / equipment layout)
e-house.drawn: Rectangle with door swings (quarter arcs at the openings) on the layout, labelled with the building tag (LER, E-house, MCC room). On a P&ID it appears only as a dashed boundary or an off-sheet reference.
e-house.notes: All buildings look alike on a plot plan: read the label. A rectangle with an AT bubble inside is an analyser-shelter; a small square with JB is a junction-box.

datasheet.form: Modular building / E-house datasheet (IEC 62271-202; A60 fire rating)

local-control-station.drawn: Field bubble marked HS (hand switch) beside the motor it starts and stops, joined to it by a dashed electrical signal line; the bubble is often annotated START / STOP or L-O-R.
local-control-station.notes: HS bubbles with a horizontal bar are on the console, not in the field. Some P&IDs omit local stations entirely; they then appear only on the electrical layout as a small rectangle at the motor.

junction-box.drawn: Small square or rectangle labelled JB plus its number, with field cables entering from the bottom and a multicore leaving towards the control room.
junction-box.notes: Appears on instrument location plans, cable block diagrams and electrical layouts, not on P&IDs. An LCS is a similar small box at a motor with push-buttons.

lighting-mast.standard: IEC 60617 (lamp: circle with ×) / lighting layout convention
lighting-mast.drawn: On lighting layouts: the lamp symbol (circle with ×) for each floodlight, drawn on a mast or pole with its mounting height noted; floodlights sometimes add an arrow or wedge for the aiming direction.
lighting-mast.notes: Circle with × is the generic IEC lamp; a status beacon on F&G layouts uses a similar lamp with rays (alarm-beacon). Lighting is not shown on P&IDs.

analyser-shelter.standard: Layout plan convention (plot plan / equipment layout) + ISA 5.1 analyser bubbles
analyser-shelter.drawn: Building rectangle with doors at each end on the layout. On the P&ID the analysers inside (AT / AE bubbles) are often drawn within a dashed boundary marked "analyser house" with sample and return lines to the process.
analyser-shelter.notes: Look for sample lines (small-bore, often with a sample cooler) running to a boundary that contains several AT bubbles. A building with no analysers is an E-house or LER.

ups-battery-cabinet.drawn: Rectifier (square with a diagonal, ~ above and = below) feeding a DC link with a battery (pairs of long and short parallel lines), then an inverter (= / ~), often with a static bypass switch drawn around them, inside a UPS boundary.
ups-battery-cabinet.notes: Square with a diagonal is the IEC converter: ~ / = is a rectifier or charger, = / ~ an inverter, ~ / ~ a frequency converter (VFD). Battery alone (long and short lines) is a DC battery bank.

vfd-cabinet.drawn: IEC converter square with a diagonal and ~ on both sides (frequency converter), in the feeder to a motor (circle with M). On P&IDs the motor may carry an SC or VSD note, and the speed signal is an SC / SIC loop.
vfd-cabinet.notes: ~ / ~ = frequency converter (VFD); ~ / = = rectifier; = / ~ = inverter. Soft starters are drawn as a box with a different note.

neutral-earthing-resistor.drawn: Rectangle (IEC resistor) in the line from the transformer or generator star point down to the earth symbol (three shortening horizontal lines), often with a CT on the neutral.
neutral-earthing-resistor.notes: IEC draws resistors as rectangles; ANSI drawings use a zig-zag. A rectangle in a neutral-to-earth connection is an NER; an earthing transformer is a zig-zag winding symbol instead.

navigation-aid.standard: Layout plan convention (plot plan / equipment layout); IALA R0139 marking
navigation-aid.drawn: On layouts: a lantern (circle) with light rays at the platform corners, labelled with its character (e.g. Mo(U) 15s, 10 nm) and a fog signal marked FOG or a horn outline.
navigation-aid.notes: Not on P&IDs. Obstruction lights on stacks and cranes are smaller red lamps; status beacons on F&G layouts are alarm-beacon.

pressure-transmitter.drawn: Plain circle (field-mounted bubble) with PT, PIT or PT plus loop number, joined by a short solid process connection line to the pipe or vessel.
pressure-transmitter.notes: A bubble with a horizontal bar across it is a DCS / control-room function (PIC, PI on the console), not a field device. PG / PI with no bar is a local gauge (pressure-gauge). PDT has two process connections (dp-transmitter). PST / PSH / PSL are switches (pressure-switch).

dp-transmitter.drawn: Field bubble with PDT (or PDIT, FT, LT) joined by two process connection lines, the high side and the low side, to two points on the pipe or vessel, e.g. either side of a filter, strainer or exchanger.
dp-transmitter.notes: Two impulse lines from one bubble = differential pressure. If the two taps straddle an orifice plate the loop is a flow measurement (orifice-flowmeter); if they are on the top and bottom of a vessel it is a DP level transmitter. ISA codes here: FT = with orifice; LT = DP level.

orifice-flowmeter.standard: ISA 5.1 (orifice plate in flanges, FE + FT)
orifice-flowmeter.drawn: Two short parallel bars across the line (the orifice flanges with the plate between them), tagged FE, with two taps to an FT or FIT bubble. Some legends draw a single bar, or a box around the line with a diagonal.
orifice-flowmeter.notes: With no transmitter and tag RO or FO it is a restriction orifice, not a meter. Venturi and flow nozzle are drawn as a converging / diverging outline instead. A flanged meter run with 10D / 5D straight lengths and a flow conditioner is still this element. ISA codes here: FO = restriction orifice.

datasheet.form: Orifice plate / flow element specification form (ISA-TR20.00.01; ISO 5167-2 calculation)

coriolis-flowmeter.standard: ISA 5.1 (flow element + transmitter); no agreed ISA element shape for Coriolis
coriolis-flowmeter.drawn: Inline box on the line, often with a U or double-U loop drawn inside, joined to an FT / FIT bubble (integral transmitter). Frequently just a generic FE box with "CORIOLIS" or "MASS" written beside it.
coriolis-flowmeter.notes: ISA 5.1 has no dedicated Coriolis element, so legends differ; read the text beside the box, the instrument index or the datasheet for the technology. Common on chemical injection, condensate, fiscal liquid and test separator outlets. ISA codes here: FQT = totaliser.

ultrasonic-flowmeter.standard: ISA 5.1 (flow element + transmitter); ultrasonic element varies by legend
ultrasonic-flowmeter.drawn: Inline spool box with transducer marks on opposite sides and a diagonal acoustic path between them, joined to an FT bubble. Many legends just write "USM" or "UFM" beside a generic FE box.
ultrasonic-flowmeter.notes: Fiscal gas metering runs (AGA 9) are usually multipath ultrasonic; a clamp-on meter is drawn on the outside of the pipe with no break in the line. Check the technology in the instrument index.

datasheet.form: Ultrasonic flowmeter specification form (ISA-TR20.00.01; AGA 9 / ISO 17089-1)

guided-wave-radar.drawn: LT / LIT field bubble on top of an external chamber (cage) bolted to the vessel by an upper and a lower connection, with a probe line hanging down inside the chamber; or the bubble sits directly on a vessel top nozzle.
guided-wave-radar.notes: A bridle (vertical standpipe) carrying several instruments is common: the LT, an LG (magnetic-level-gauge) and LSHH / LSLL switches all hang off it. Non-contact radar uses the same LT bubble without a probe. Interface level is LT with the service written beside it.

magnetic-level-gauge.drawn: Tall narrow chamber beside the vessel with an upper and a lower side connection (isolation valves on each, vent on top, drain below), labelled with an LG or LI bubble.
magnetic-level-gauge.notes: Same chamber with a transmitter strapped on is LG plus LT on one bridle (set transmitter). A plain glass (reflex / transparent) gauge is drawn the same and is also tagged LG; check the datasheet.

temperature-transmitter.drawn: TT or TIT field bubble joined to a thermowell (a short U-shaped pocket pushed into the pipe, sometimes tagged TW), on the pipe or vessel.
temperature-transmitter.notes: TE (element) plus TT (transmitter) of the same loop are one physical item. TI / TG with no transmitter is a dial thermometer (temperature-gauge). A TW bubble on its own is a spare or test thermowell.

datasheet.form: Temperature transmitter + thermowell specification forms (ISA-TR20.00.01; ASME PTC 19.3 TW)

pressure-gauge.drawn: Field bubble marked PI (or PG on some legends) joined to the pipe by a short process line; no signal line leaves it, because it is a local dial.
pressure-gauge.notes: Same bubble as a transmitter but with PI / PG and no signal line. A bubble with a bar through it reading PI is a console indication, not a gauge. PDI / PDG across a filter is a differential gauge.

datasheet.form: Pressure gauge specification form (ISA-TR20.00.01; EN 837-1 / ASME B40.100)

temperature-gauge.drawn: Field bubble marked TI (or TG) on a thermowell pocket in the pipe; no signal line.
temperature-gauge.notes: Same as the temperature transmitter but with TI / TG. A test thermowell with no instrument is a TW bubble alone.

datasheet.form: Bimetal thermometer + thermowell specification forms (ISA-TR20.00.01; ASME B40.200)

magnetic-flowmeter.standard: ISA 5.1 (flow element + transmitter); magnetic element drawn as a box or circle with M
magnetic-flowmeter.drawn: Inline box (or circle) on the line marked M, joined to an FT bubble. Some legends use a generic FE with "MAG" written beside it.
magnetic-flowmeter.notes: Only for conductive liquids (water, produced water, seawater, chemicals); a meter on a gas line is never a mag meter. A circle with M on a valve stem is a motor actuator, not a flowmeter.

vortex-flowmeter.standard: ISA 5.1 (flow element + transmitter); vortex element varies by legend
vortex-flowmeter.drawn: Inline box with a small bluff-body triangle (the shedder bar) and wavy vortex lines downstream, joined to an FT bubble. Often a generic FE with "VORTEX" written beside it.
vortex-flowmeter.notes: Used on steam, fuel gas, utility gas and clean liquids. Read the instrument index to confirm the technology when the legend only gives a generic flow element.

level-switch.drawn: Field bubble with LS plus H / HH / L / LL (LSH, LSHH, LSLL) on a side connection of a vessel or bridle at the trip height. In a SIS it is often drawn with a diamond or hexagon tag for the logic it feeds.
level-switch.notes: S = switch, so the bubble has no transmitter letter T. Trip levels are written beside it in mm or %. Vibrating fork, float and displacer switches all use the same bubble.

pressure-switch.drawn: Field bubble with PS plus H / HH / L / LL (PSH, PSHH, PSL, PSLL) on a short process connection, usually feeding a trip.
pressure-switch.notes: Switches have S as the function letter and no T. A PSV is a relief valve, not a switch: PSV has V for valve. PDSH across a filter is a differential pressure switch.

vibration-probe.drawn: A VE or VT bubble joined to a small square or dot on a motor, pump, compressor or bearing outline, often in A / B or X / Y pairs, feeding VI / VA / VSHH functions in the DCS, SIS or CMS.
vibration-probe.notes: V as the first letter is vibration (ISA 5.1). One vibration-probe per monitored bearing; pair for X-Y proximity probes, kind accelerometer for casing sensors. ZE on a machine is an axial position probe and maps here too. Voting such as 1oo2 between A and B means two sensors exist.

control-console.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064)
control-console.drawn: Plan view: a run of desk segments (straight, angled or curved) with the monitor line along the back edge and operator chairs as circles in front, laid out facing the video wall.
control-console.notes: Only on control room layouts. A straight table with a chair is a desk; a grid of tiles on a wall is the video wall.

video-wall.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064)
video-wall.drawn: Elevation: a grid of display tiles (rows × columns) on a frame with a base cabinet; in plan, a long thin rectangle along the CCR wall with the viewing distance to the consoles dimensioned.

door.standard: Architectural plan convention (door swing); IMO FTP Code fire ratings
door.drawn: Plan view: a gap in the wall with the door leaf drawn as a line at 90° and a quarter-circle arc for the swing; double doors have two leaves and arcs, sliding doors a leaf parallel to the wall. The fire rating (A60, H120) is noted on the door schedule.
door.notes: Arc = hinged door; the hinge side is the arc centre. Blast doors are drawn thicker; roller shutters as a dashed line across the opening.

datasheet.form: Door schedule (IMO FTP Code A60 / H120, EN 1125 / EN 1154 hardware)

window.standard: Architectural plan convention (window in wall); IMO FTP Code fire ratings
window.drawn: Plan view: the wall is interrupted and parallel thin lines across the opening show the glazing; sill height and fire / blast rating are on the window schedule.
window.notes: A gap with an arc is a door; a gap with thin parallel lines is a window.

datasheet.form: Window schedule (IMO FTP Code A60 / H120, ISO 3903)

room.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064)
room.drawn: Plan view: double-line walls enclosing the room with door and window openings and the room name and number written inside; raised floors noted RAF with the floor height.
room.notes: Rooms are background for consoles, cabinets and furniture. A single building rectangle on a plot plan is an e-house or module.

datasheet.form: Room data sheet (ISO 11064-3; EN 12825 raised floor)

system-cabinet.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064) / equipment room layout
system-cabinet.drawn: Plan view: a row of squares (cabinets) against a wall or back to back, with door swing arcs on the front and the system (DCS, SIS, F&G, marshalling) written on each; front and rear access clearances dashed.
system-cabinet.notes: Only on equipment-room layouts. Switchgear line-ups look similar but are deeper and labelled with feeders.

datasheet.form: Cabinet layout / system cabinet specification (IEC 61439, IEC 60297)

operator-chair.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064) (furniture)
operator-chair.drawn: Plan view: a rounded seat square with a curved backrest and armrests, placed at a console or desk; often just a circle.
operator-chair.notes: Furniture appears only on control room and office layouts.

desk.standard: Layout plan convention (architectural / control room layout, ISO 11064) (furniture)
desk.drawn: Plan view: a rectangle (desk or table) with monitors drawn as thick lines along the back edge and chairs as circles or seat shapes around it.
desk.notes: A curved or angled run of desks with many monitors is a control-console.

wall-display.standard: Layout plan convention (control room / instrument layout)
wall-display.drawn: Control room or equipment-room layout: a thin rectangle on the wall (plan) or a framed screen on a bracket (elevation), labelled with its size and content.
wall-display.notes: A single screen; a grid of tiles is the video wall.

cctv-camera.standard: Security / telecom layout convention (camera with field of view)
cctv-camera.drawn: Telecom layout: a camera symbol (small box with a lens) with its field-of-view wedge drawn dashed in the direction it looks; PTZ cameras marked PTZ with a full circle of coverage.
cctv-camera.notes: A wedge from a camera box is the CCTV view; a wedge from a circle with F is a flame detector cone. Not on P&IDs.

fire-alarm-panel.standard: F&G / safety layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); EN 54-2
fire-alarm-panel.drawn: On F&G block diagrams and room layouts: a rectangle labelled FACP, F&G or ESD with the zones it serves; detectors and call points are wired to it in loops.
fire-alarm-panel.notes: An F&G or ESD mimic panel in the CCR; the logic itself lives in the system cabinets (system-cabinet).

datasheet.form: Fire alarm control panel datasheet (EN 54-2 / IEC 61511)

pedestal-crane.standard: Layout plan convention (lifting / materials-handling study); API Spec 2C
pedestal-crane.drawn: Plan view: the pedestal as a circle at the crane position with the maximum (and minimum) working radius drawn as large dashed circles around it, the boom as a line, and laydown areas and lift paths inside the radius; tagged CR- with SWL at radius.
pedestal-crane.notes: The large dashed reach circle is the clue. A small post with a short jib and no reach study is a davit-crane. Not on P&IDs, except a diesel or hydraulic utility tie-in.

shipping-container.drawn: Plan view: a rectangle at the ISO footprint (10, 20 or 40 ft) in a laydown area, often with a diagonal cross meaning "laydown / temporary", the door end marked by a thicker line, and its size written inside.
shipping-container.notes: Laydown areas are rectangles with a cross or hatch; a container is one sized like an ISO box. Baskets are open and smaller; tote tanks are near-square.

cargo-basket.drawn: Elevation: an open-topped frame with mesh sides hanging from a four-leg sling set to a master link; in plan, a long rectangle in the laydown area.
cargo-basket.notes: Open top and mesh sides tell it from a closed container. Not on P&IDs.

monorail-hoist.drawn: Plan view: a dash-dot or thick line along the runway beam labelled "monorail, SWL x t" from the equipment it serves to the drop or laydown zone; in elevation a beam with a trolley, hoist block and hook.
monorail-hoist.notes: Shown on mechanical handling and layout drawings over pumps, compressors and exchangers that need lifting. Not on P&IDs.

lifeboat-davit.standard: Layout plan convention (lifting / materials-handling study) (lifesaving appliance plan); SOLAS LSA Code
lifeboat-davit.drawn: On escape and lifesaving plans: a boat outline (pointed or rounded ends) at the muster station, under davit arms, with its capacity (e.g. 50 P) written inside; often marked TEMPSC.
lifeboat-davit.notes: Liferafts are drawn as small circles or canisters. Never on P&IDs.

datasheet.form: Lifeboat and davit certificate / schedule (SOLAS LSA Code IV/4.6, VI/6.1)

tote-tank.standard: Layout plan convention (lifting / materials-handling study) / P&ID (temporary chemical supply)
tote-tank.drawn: Layout: a near-square frame with the tank outline inside, in the chemical laydown; on P&IDs a small vessel or "tote" box with a hose connection to the chemical injection skid suction.
tote-tank.notes: A permanent chemical tank is part of the chemical-injection-skid. Totes are temporary, hose-connected supplies.

davit-crane.drawn: Elevation: a post curving into a short jib with a hook; in plan, a small circle with a short reach radius (dashed) over the item it serves, labelled with SWL.
davit-crane.notes: Small reach circle (a few metres) versus the large reach of a pedestal crane. Not on P&IDs.

gas-cylinder-quad.standard: Layout plan convention (lifting / materials-handling study) / P&ID (bottle rack)
gas-cylinder-quad.drawn: Layout: a square frame filled with small circles (the cylinders). On P&IDs a bottle rack is drawn as one or more small capsules joined to a manifold with a regulator (PCV) on the outlet.
gas-cylinder-quad.notes: Nitrogen back-up racks and calibration gas bottles use the same drawing; read the gas. A nitrogen generator package is a separate item.

marine-loading-arm.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 / OCIMF loading arm convention
marine-loading-arm.drawn: An articulated line from the jetty riser through swivel joints (small circles) at the base, apex and outboard end, ending in the emergency release coupling (two close bars with valves) and the ship manifold flange; a counterweight box on the inboard arm.
marine-loading-arm.notes: Swivels plus the ERS mark tell it from a hose. Truck loading arms are smaller and drawn with the truck outline. ISA codes here: XV = ERS.

truck-loading-bay.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 + ISA 5.1 metering / layout convention for the bay
truck-loading-bay.drawn: Per bay: block valve, strainer, meter (FE / FQ, often PD), digital set-stop control valve and the loading arm or hose dropping to a road tanker outline; on the plot plan, lanes under a canopy rectangle.
truck-loading-bay.notes: A meter run ending at a tanker outline is the clue. Marine loading uses articulated arms to a ship manifold instead.

datasheet.form: Loading bay specification (API RP 1004 / EN 13083, API 2610)

pipeline-valve-station.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 / pipeline P&ID convention (ASME B31.8)
pipeline-valve-station.drawn: A mainline ball valve below the grade line with its stem extended up to an above-grade actuator (rectangle: gas-over-oil or electric), and blowdown / bypass branches rising to their own valves; often within a fenced compound outline.
pipeline-valve-station.notes: The grade line with a buried valve and stem extension identifies it. Topsides ESDVs are esd-valve.

datasheet.form: Pipeline valve datasheet (API 6D / ISO 14313) + actuator sheet

packaged-boiler.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (boiler / fired steam generator)
packaged-boiler.drawn: A horizontal shell (capsule) with fire tubes drawn as parallel lines inside, a burner box with the fuel line on the front end, a flue stack on top, steam outlet from the top and feedwater inlet; often inside a package boundary with the feedwater pumps.
packaged-boiler.notes: Shell with tubes plus burner and stack = fire-tube boiler. A fired heater is a vertical firebox with a process coil; a TEG reboiler is a smaller fire-tube capsule inside a regeneration package.

datasheet.form: Steam boiler datasheet (EN 12953 / ASME Section I)

oily-water-separator.drawn: An open rectangular basin (no top line) with inclined parallel plates drawn as slanted lines in the middle, an inlet chamber with a baffle, an oil skimmer or weir to the oil outlet, a sludge draw-off at the bottom and the clean water outlet over a weir at the far end.
oily-water-separator.notes: Slanted plate pack in an open basin = CPI / plate interceptor. A closed horizontal vessel with weirs is a separator; produced water offshore uses hydrocyclones and degassers instead.

bund-wall.drawn: Plot plan: a double-line rectangle (the wall thickness) enclosing the tank outline, with the bund drain sump in a corner and a normally closed drain valve outside the wall; the bund capacity and wall height are noted.
bund-wall.notes: A double-line enclosure around tanks = bund. On P&IDs only the bund drain line and its locked-closed valve appear.

perimeter-fence.drawn: Site plan: a line with crosses at intervals (—x—x—) along the boundary, gates shown as a swing (leaf and arc) or a sliding leaf, with fence height and type noted.
perimeter-fence.notes: Only on site plans. The crosses tell it from a wall (solid double line) or a kerb.

hv-circuit-breaker.drawn: Single-line: a switch blade (a line at an angle) with a small × on the fixed contact, in the feeder between busbar and line or transformer; often drawn inside a bay with disconnectors on either side.
hv-circuit-breaker.notes: IEC symbols: × on the contact = circuit breaker; a bar across the contact = disconnector; a blade to the earth symbol = earthing switch. ANSI drawings use a square box with device number 52. QA / QB / QC are IEC 81346-2 class letters for breaker, disconnector and earthing switch.

disconnector.drawn: Single-line: a switch blade with a short bar across the fixed contact (disconnector), usually next to an earthing switch drawn as a second blade going to the earth symbol (three shortening lines).
disconnector.notes: Bar on the contact = disconnector (isolator, no load breaking); × = circuit breaker. Some drawings tag disconnectors DS. ANSI device numbers are 89 for the disconnector and 57 for the earthing switch.

instrument-transformer.drawn: Single-line: a current transformer is a small circle threaded on the primary conductor (or a loop) with its secondary leads; a voltage transformer is a pair of small overlapping circles connected from the line to earth. A CVT adds a capacitor stack (two parallel plates) above the VT.
instrument-transformer.notes: Circle on the line = CT; two circles from line to earth = VT. Small overlapping circles in a feeder (not to earth) are a power transformer. CT also collides with cooling-tower tags on process drawings: context decides.

surge-arrester.drawn: Single-line: a rectangle (non-linear resistor) with an arrow inside pointing to earth, connected from the line to the earth symbol, usually at transformer terminals and line entries.
surge-arrester.notes: Rectangle with an internal arrow to earth = surge arrester; a plain rectangle to earth on a neutral is a neutral earthing resistor. LA (lightning arrester) is an older name.

busbar-gantry.standard: IEC 60617 (single-line diagram) (busbar); layout elevation for the gantry steel
busbar-gantry.drawn: Single-line: a thick horizontal line (busbar) with bay connections dropping from it at dots; on substation layouts and elevations the gantry is a pair of lattice columns with a girder carrying strain insulator strings and the bus conductors.
busbar-gantry.notes: A thick line with feeders = busbar. Double-busbar stations show two parallel thick lines with a coupler bay between them.

industrial-building.standard: Layout plan convention (site plan / architectural plan)
industrial-building.drawn: Site or floor plan: a rectangle on the structural grid (dash-dot), with roller-shutter doors shown as dashed lines across openings and personnel doors as swing arcs; the building name and use are written inside.
industrial-building.notes: Buildings are identified by label on plot plans; an E-house or analyser shelter is smaller and skid-based. Not on P&IDs.

datasheet.form: Building specification (EN 1993-1-1 frame, EN 14509 cladding, EN 13241 doors)

gatehouse.drawn: Site plan: a small hut rectangle on a kerbed island beside the lane, a boom barrier drawn as a thick line from a pivot across the lane, and lane direction arrows.
gatehouse.notes: Only on site and security plans.

chemical-injection-skid.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents)
chemical-injection-skid.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary containing a small storage tank, a suction header and one or more metering pumps (small circles with a diagonal arrow), with injection lines (CI / MI, ½"–1") leaving to the injection points, each with a check valve and isolation at the quill.
chemical-injection-skid.notes: The chemical (demulsifier, corrosion inhibitor, scale inhibitor, methanol, biocide) is written on the tank or on the outgoing lines. Vendor packages are often a single box with only the battery-limit connections shown.

metering-skid.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents); ISA 5.1 FE / FQ
metering-skid.drawn: Dash-dot boundary with an inlet header and outlet header joined by parallel meter runs; each run has an inlet block valve, strainer, flow element (FE / FQ, ultrasonic or turbine) with PT and TT, and an outlet valve; a prover connection and sampler may be shown.
metering-skid.notes: Parallel identical runs between two headers are the signature. A single flowmeter in a line is an instrument, not a metering skid; a compact prover (X-R155 type) is a separate box connected by the prover loop. ISA codes here: AT = sampler / densitometer.

datasheet.form: Fiscal metering system datasheet (API MPMS Ch. 4 / 5, AGA 9 / ISO 17089-1)

instrument-air-package.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents)
instrument-air-package.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary containing an air compressor (screw symbol or generic compressor), a twin-tower desiccant dryer (two tall capsules side by side), filters, and the air receiver (vertical vessel) before the instrument-air (IA) header.
instrument-air-package.notes: Two identical tall capsules side by side = dryer towers. Often only the package box with IA outlet and the receiver are shown on the utilities P&ID. ISA codes here: AT = dew point.

datasheet.form: Instrument air package datasheet (ISO 8573-1 class, ISO 1217 capacity)

teg-regeneration.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents)
teg-regeneration.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary with a horizontal reboiler (capsule with a U-shaped fire tube drawn inside), a short packed still column standing on top of it with the vent to atmosphere, a surge drum and lean-glycol pumps; rich TEG in, lean TEG out to the contactor.
teg-regeneration.notes: The reboiler with a fire-tube and a vertical still on top is the clue. The tall TEG contactor column itself is a separate item (column).

hydraulic-power-unit.standard: ISO 1219-1 fluid power symbols in a package boundary
hydraulic-power-unit.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary with an open reservoir (U-shaped tank), hydraulic pumps (circle with a filled triangle pointing outward on the outlet), filters, accumulators (vertical capsules with a dividing line) and the HP / LP supply headers leaving as hydraulic lines.
hydraulic-power-unit.notes: ISO 1219 symbols (filled triangle in a circle = hydraulic pump; capsule with a line = accumulator) identify a hydraulic system. The WHCP sits downstream with one line per actuator.

datasheet.form: Hydraulic power unit datasheet (ISO 4413 / API 6A control systems)

nitrogen-generator.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents)
nitrogen-generator.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary with air filters (diamond with a dashed line), an air heater, membrane modules (rectangles with a diagonal dashed membrane line, permeate vented to atmosphere) and a nitrogen receiver before the N2 outlet.
nitrogen-generator.notes: Membrane modules with a vent line identify the generator; a nitrogen bottle rack is a gas-cylinder-quad. Often shown on the utilities P&ID as a single package box. ISA codes here: AT = O2.

datasheet.form: Nitrogen generator package datasheet (ISO 8573-1 feed air; ASME VIII-1 receiver)

hydrocyclone-package.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents); cyclone convention
hydrocyclone-package.drawn: Horizontal vessel(s) with cyclone liners drawn as long cones (or a single inverted cone, the generic cyclone symbol), produced water in at the inlet header, clean water out, and the oily reject to the reject header controlled by a PDV / PDIC ratio loop.
hydrocyclone-package.notes: Cones inside a vessel = hydrocyclones (or a desander if on the well stream with a sand accumulator). Reject-ratio control is the PDIC loop between inlet, outlet and reject.

compact-prover.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 / API MPMS Ch. 4.2 prover convention
compact-prover.drawn: A horizontal flow tube with a piston (displacer) drawn inside and two detector switches on top marking the calibrated volume, connected by a prover loop with valves to the metering skid; often just a box labelled "prover".
compact-prover.notes: Piston in a tube with detector marks = compact prover; a long U-shaped pipe loop with spheres is a conventional ball prover. ISA codes here: ZS = detector.

water-filter-package.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents) (filter: vessel crossed by a dashed medium line)
water-filter-package.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary with two to four vertical filter vessels in parallel between inlet and outlet headers, each crossed by dashed lines for the media bed, plus backwash and air-scour headers with butterfly valves.
water-filter-package.notes: Parallel identical filter vessels with backwash lines = multimedia filter package. A single cartridge housing is cartridge-filter.

datasheet.form: Filter package datasheet (AWWA B100 / ASME VIII-1)

hypochlorite-generator.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (package boundary with contents) + IEC 60617 rectifier
hypochlorite-generator.drawn: Dash-dot package boundary with a seawater strainer, electrolyser cells (boxes with parallel electrode plates) fed from a DC rectifier (square with diagonal, ~ / =), a degassing tank venting hydrogen, and hypochlorite dosing out to the seawater caissons.
hypochlorite-generator.notes: Electrolyser cells plus a rectifier identify it; a chemical-injection-skid has a tank and metering pumps instead. ISA codes here: AT = H2.

weld-neck-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar
weld-neck-flange.drawn: In section: a flange disc with a long tapered hub narrowing to the pipe wall and a butt weld at the hub end. On P&IDs just a short bar across the line; on isometrics a bar with a weld dot.
weld-neck-flange.notes: The flange type comes from the piping class, not the P&ID. The long taper identifies weld-neck; slip-on and socket-weld have short hubs; lap-joint has a loose ring on a stub end.

datasheet.form: Piping class / flange bill of materials (ASME B16.5 / B16.47)

slip-on-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar
slip-on-flange.drawn: In section: a flange with a short hub slid over the pipe, the pipe end set back from the face, with fillet welds inside the bore and at the hub. On P&IDs a short bar across the line.
slip-on-flange.notes: Pipe passing into the flange bore with two fillet welds = slip-on. Weld-neck has a long tapered hub and one butt weld.

datasheet.form: Piping class / flange bill of materials (ASME B16.5)

socket-weld-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar; ASME B16.11 socket
socket-weld-flange.drawn: In section: a small-bore flange with a socket the pipe slides into against a shoulder (small gap at the bottom), and one fillet weld at the hub. On P&IDs a short bar on a small-bore (≤ 2") line.
socket-weld-flange.notes: Socket-weld is small-bore only (NPS ½–3). Threaded flanges show thread hatching in the bore instead of a weld.

datasheet.form: Piping class / flange bill of materials (ASME B16.5, B16.11)

threaded-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar; ASME B1.20.1 NPT
threaded-flange.drawn: In section: a flange with a short hub and thread marks (zig-zag) in the bore where the pipe screws in, sometimes with a seal weld. On P&IDs a short bar, usually on utility or small-bore lines.
threaded-flange.notes: Zig-zag thread lines in the bore identify it. Most offshore hydrocarbon piping classes do not allow threaded joints; expect it on utility water or air.

datasheet.form: Piping class / flange bill of materials (ASME B16.5, B1.20.1)

lap-joint-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar; MSS SP-43 stub end
lap-joint-flange.drawn: In section: a stub end (pipe with a flared lap at the face) with a loose backing flange sitting behind the lap, not welded to the pipe. On P&IDs a short bar like any flange.
lap-joint-flange.notes: The loose ring behind a lap identifies it. Used on stainless or alloy lines where the backing flange can be carbon steel, and where bolt holes must be lined up after welding.

datasheet.form: Piping class / flange bill of materials (ASME B16.5, MSS SP-43)

swivel-ring-flange.standard: ASME B16.5 flange types drawn in half-section (GA / isometric detail convention); on P&IDs every flange is a short bar; MSS SP-44 / pipeline convention
swivel-ring-flange.drawn: In section: a weld hub carrying the gasket face with a separate loose ring that can rotate around it to align bolt holes; drawn with a curved arrow on some pipeline tie-in details. On P&IDs a flange bar, often at a riser or spool tie-in.
swivel-ring-flange.notes: Found at subsea and riser tie-ins where bolt-hole alignment is hard. On P&IDs it is indistinguishable from other flanges; read the tie-in detail.

datasheet.form: Pipeline flange datasheet (ASME B16.5 drilling, MSS SP-44)

olet.standard: ISO 10628-2 branch connection / MSS SP-97 (isometric detail)
olet.drawn: On P&IDs a branch is just a line meeting another line with a dot (like a tee); on isometrics a branch outlet is a small saddle-shaped boss on the run pipe with the branch rising from it, noted WOL, SOL, TOL, NOL, EOL or LOL.
olet.notes: P&IDs do not distinguish an olet from a tee: the piping class branch table decides (small branches off large runs are olets). Instrument connections and vents and drains are usually olets.

datasheet.form: Piping class branch table / bill of materials (MSS SP-97)

small-bore-fitting.standard: Isometric / piping class convention (ASME B16.11); P&IDs show only the connection
small-bore-fitting.drawn: Not drawn as a separate item on P&IDs: small-bore vents, drains and instrument connections appear as short ¾"–2" lines off the main line. On isometrics the forged fitting (elbow, tee, coupling, union, cap, plug, swage) is drawn with SW or THD weld / thread marks and called up in the bill of materials.
small-bore-fitting.notes: A short NPS ≤ 2 branch with a valve and cap or plug (vent / drain) on a P&ID is made of these fittings. Class 3000 / 6000 comes from the piping class.

datasheet.form: Piping class / small-bore bill of materials (ASME B16.11, MSS SP-83 / SP-95)

expansion-joint.drawn: A short section of the line drawn with a zig-zag (convoluted) outline between two flange bars; tie rods, hinges or gimbals are noted as EJ type, often tagged EJ or XJ.
expansion-joint.notes: Zig-zag outline in the line = bellows; a flexible hose is drawn as a wavy line. Found on exhaust ducts, cooling water, compressor and turbine connections.

flexible-hose.drawn: A wavy (sinusoidal) line between two end connections, sometimes with "FH" or the hose type noted; drilling rotary hoses and loading hoses are drawn the same way.
flexible-hose.notes: Wavy line = flexible hose; a zig-zag outline = bellows expansion-joint. Some legends tag hoses FH, which clashes with fire hydrants.

datasheet.form: Hose assembly datasheet (ISO 10380 / EN 14585-1; API 16C rotary)

hammer-union.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (union) / well-testing temporary flowline convention
hammer-union.drawn: A union symbol (two short bars with a third bar between them) in the line, with the figure number (e.g. Fig 1502) noted; well-test and frac schematics show one at every temporary flowline joint.
hammer-union.notes: A flanged joint has two bars only. Figure numbers are not interchangeable (1502 vs 602 vs 2002 pressure ratings), so read the note.

datasheet.form: Temporary flowline equipment list (union figure number, API 6A service)

insulating-joint.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 / pipeline cathodic protection convention
insulating-joint.drawn: Two heavy bars across the line with a gap and a zig-zag or hatch between them, labelled IJ or IK (insulating kit), at the boundary between a cathodically protected pipeline and topsides or plant piping.
insulating-joint.notes: Found where a pipeline or riser meets the plant. Plain double bars are an ordinary flanged joint; a monolithic IJ is a weld-in item, an insulating gasket kit is a flange pair with an IK note.

rupture-disc.drawn: A curved disc (arc) between two flange bars across the relief line, usually vertical with the inlet below, tagged PSE with the burst pressure; often fitted under a PSV with a pressure gauge or switch between them.
rupture-disc.notes: An arc between flange bars with no spring = rupture disc; a spring zig-zag = PSV. A disc under a PSV forms a combination device; the PI / PSH in the space between detects a leak or burst.

datasheet.form: Rupture disc datasheet (ISO 4126-2 / API 520 Part I)

restriction-orifice.drawn: A plate across the line (one bar, or a bar with the bore gap at the centre) between two flange bars, tagged RO or FO with the bore size, and no transmitter or taps; multi-stage ROs show several plates in a row.
restriction-orifice.notes: With two taps to an FT bubble it is an orifice-flowmeter; without taps it is a restriction orifice. Common downstream of a BDV, in minimum-flow bypasses and on purge lines.

datasheet.form: Restriction orifice datasheet (ASME MFC-14M / ISO 5167-2 plate geometry)

steam-trap.drawn: A small square (or circle) in the condensate line marked T or ST, often preceded by a strainer and followed by a check valve and a test valve, at the low point of a steam line.
steam-trap.notes: Box with T on a steam or condensate line = steam trap. Some legends tag traps TR, which clashes with transformer tags.

drain-hub.drawn: A funnel (V or trapezoid) open at the top with the drain pipe leaving the bottom to the open-drain (OD) header; drawn below the vents and drains of equipment that discharge into it.
drain-hub.notes: A funnel feeding an OD line = open drain hub or tundish. Closed drains (CD) are piped directly with no funnel.

datasheet.form: Open drain item schedule (ISO 13702 / API RP 14C drain systems)

pipe-spool.drawn: A solid line labelled with its line number (size-service-number-class-insulation, e.g. 8"-PG-2101-D6A-N); flanged joints appear as short double bars across the line. Insulation is marked by the H / IH suffix or a dashed outline along the line.
pipe-spool.notes: Process lines are thick solid; utility and minor lines thinner; instrument signal lines are dashed (electrical) or with hash marks (pneumatic). Each line number between two nozzles becomes one spool run.

datasheet.form: Line list / piping class (ASME B31.3, B36.10)

elbow.standard: ISO 6412 / isometric convention (fittings are not shown individually on P&IDs)
elbow.drawn: On P&IDs a change of direction is just a corner in the line; elbows are only drawn on isometrics and GA drawings, as a bend or a corner with a short tick at each weld.
elbow.notes: Take the angle and radius (LR / SR) from the isometric or the piping class, not the P&ID. Treat a P&ID corner as an elbow only when building a 3D route.

datasheet.form: Piping class / isometric bill of materials (ASME B16.9)

tee.drawn: A branch line meeting a run line; a dot at the junction confirms a connection (lines crossing without a dot or with a gap / hop are not connected).
tee.notes: Reducing tees are shown by the different line sizes of run and branch. Crossing lines without a dot are not a tee. On isometrics the tee is drawn with weld ticks.

datasheet.form: Piping class / isometric bill of materials (ASME B16.9)

reducer.drawn: A trapezoid in the line, the large end facing the larger pipe, with the two sizes written beside it (e.g. 8"×6"). Eccentric reducers have one flat side, noted FOT (flat on top) or FOB (flat on bottom).
reducer.notes: A size change at a valve or pump nozzle is often shown only by the size note. Eccentric FOT reducers sit on pump suctions.

datasheet.form: Piping class / isometric bill of materials (ASME B16.9)

flanged-joint.drawn: Two short parallel bars across the line (a flange pair), sometimes with a gap between them; at a nozzle only one bar is drawn against the equipment.
flanged-joint.notes: Two bars with a filled or open paddle between them, or with a figure-8 drawn beside them on a short stem, is a spectacle blind or spade (not a plain joint); two bars with taps and an FE tag is an orifice flange pair. Spec breaks (class changes) are marked at a flange with the two class codes.

datasheet.form: Piping class (ASME B16.5 / B16.47 flanges, B16.20 gaskets)

blind-flange.drawn: A line ending in a flange bar followed by a thicker solid bar (or a filled half-circle cap): a blinded end or spare connection.
blind-flange.notes: A single solid bar across the line between two flange bars is a spade / blind in the line; a figure-8 is a spectacle blind. A line ending with a plain dome is a pipe cap (welded), not a blind.

spectacle-blind.drawn: A figure-8 drawn across the line between two flange bars: one circle filled (solid blind) and one open (spacer ring). The filled half on the line means the line is blinded (normally closed); the open half on the line means it is open.
spectacle-blind.notes: Note NO / NC (or SO / SC) beside it for the normal position. Many legends draw the figure-8 beside the flange pair on a short stem instead of across the line: the circle next to the stem is the half in the line (open ring = open, blank = closed), and the blank may be hatched or drawn as concentric circles. A single filled paddle is a spade; a single open ring is a spacer.

datasheet.form: Piping class / special item datasheet (ASME B16.48)

y-strainer.drawn: A Y-shaped leg slanting down from the line with a dashed line inside it for the screen, sometimes tagged SP / Y-STR with a blow-down valve on the end of the leg.
y-strainer.notes: A basket or temporary cone strainer is drawn as a box or cone in the line with a dashed screen. A PDI / PDT across it monitors blockage. ISA codes here: PDI = across.

basket-strainer.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (strainer: body with a dashed screen)
basket-strainer.drawn: A pot-shaped body in the line (inlet and outlet near the top) with a dashed U-shaped basket inside and a bolted cover on top; often a PDI / PDT across it.
basket-strainer.notes: A Y-shaped leg is a y-strainer; a cone in the line is a temporary strainer. Twin (duplex) basket strainers are two pots with a changeover valve.

pipe-support.standard: Piping support convention (isometric / GA support marks); MSS SP-58
pipe-support.drawn: On isometrics and GAs: a mark at the support point with its type code (shoe, guide G, line stop LS, anchor A, dummy leg DL, trunnion) and number; in section, the pipe resting on a shoe on a steel member or post.
pipe-support.notes: Not on P&IDs. An anchor is often drawn as a cross on the pipe; a guide as two short bars either side; a shoe as a small rectangle under the pipe.

datasheet.form: Pipe support schedule (MSS SP-58 / ASME B31.3)

sight-glass.drawn: A circle in the line between two flange bars, often with a small flapper or ball drawn inside, tagged FG (flow glass / sight flow indicator).
sight-glass.notes: A circle in the line tagged FG is a sight glass; an LG on a vessel is a level gauge; a circle with M is a mag meter or motor.

datasheet.form: Sight flow indicator datasheet (ASME B16.5 / B31.3)

utility-station.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (utility station / hose connections)
utility-station.drawn: A group of utility drops (plant air UA, utility water UW, nitrogen N) each with an isolation valve, a check valve and a hose connection (small triangle or coupling) at the end, boxed or noted "US-xx" on the utility P&ID.
utility-station.notes: Usually shown once in detail on a typical sheet and then as a small labelled circle or box at each location on layouts.

datasheet.form: Utility station schedule (NORSOK L-002, ISO 14726 colour codes)

gasket.standard: Piping class item (ASME B16.20 / B16.21); not drawn on P&IDs
gasket.drawn: Not drawn on P&IDs; on isometrics and joint details it is the thin element between two flange faces (a filled strip in section), called up in the bill of materials by type (SW, RTJ, sheet).
gasket.notes: Type follows the piping class: spiral-wound for RF flanges, RTJ ring for ring-joint flanges (high pressure), sheet for FF / low-pressure utility.

datasheet.form: Piping class / gasket specification (ASME B16.20 / B16.21)

stud-bolt-set.standard: Piping class item (ASME B16.5 bolting, ASTM A193 / A194); not drawn on P&IDs
stud-bolt-set.drawn: Not drawn on P&IDs; in joint details, studs are lines through both flanges with a hex nut at each end, specified in the bill of materials by number, diameter and length.
stud-bolt-set.notes: Quantity and size come from ASME B16.5 tables for the NPS and class; coating from the piping or coating specification.

datasheet.form: Piping class / bolting specification (ASME B16.5, ASTM A193 B7 / A194 2H)

pipe-clamp.standard: Piping support convention (isometric / support detail); MSS SP-58 / SP-69
pipe-clamp.drawn: Not on P&IDs. On support drawings and isometrics a hanger is marked at the support point with its type (e.g. a rod hanger with a clamp, MSS type 3 or 4), and in detail the pipe circle is shown gripped by the clamp straps hanging from a rod.
pipe-clamp.notes: A clamp hanging on a rod is a hanger; a shoe on steel is a pipe-support. Riser clamps carry vertical pipe at floor penetrations.

gas-turbine-generator.drawn: Gas turbine drawn as a narrowing trapezoid (compressor), a small combustor box with the fuel line into it, and a widening trapezoid (turbine) with the exhaust leaving, coupled by the shaft to a circle with G (generator).
gas-turbine-generator.notes: On electrical single-line diagrams only the generator circle with G and ~ appears. A turbine coupled to a compressor instead of G is a turbine-driven compressor (centrifugal-compressor with driver gas-turbine). A box marked DE with G is a diesel generator.

datasheet.form: API 616 gas turbine datasheet (+ IEC 60034-3 generator)

centrifugal-compressor.drawn: Trapezoid (wide end = suction, narrow end = discharge) with the driver on the shaft: a circle with M for a motor, or a gas turbine drawn as a second, reversed trapezoid. Anti-surge recycle and a recycle valve usually loop from discharge back to suction.
centrifugal-compressor.notes: Trapezoid = dynamic compressor. A trapezoid narrowing the other way, coupled to a generator or compressor, is a turbine (or an expander). A rectangle with a piston is a reciprocating compressor; two meshing rotors mean a screw compressor.

reciprocating-compressor.drawn: Cylinder (rectangle) with a piston and rod inside, the rod running to a crank; suction usually into the top and discharge out of the bottom, with suction and discharge pulsation bottles drawn as small horizontal vessels on each nozzle.
reciprocating-compressor.notes: Multi-stage machines show one cylinder per stage with interstage coolers and scrubbers between them. A trapezoid is a centrifugal compressor.

screw-compressor.drawn: Casing outline with two meshing rotors (two overlapping circles or intermeshing helices) inside, driver on the shaft. Packaged instrument-air or gas-boost units are usually shown inside a dashed package boundary with the oil separator and cooler.
screw-compressor.notes: Two rotors = rotary screw (or lobe) compressor. A trapezoid is centrifugal; a piston in a cylinder is reciprocating. Oil-free air packages (instrument-air-package) use the same compressor symbol inside a larger package.

datasheet.form: API 619 rotary-type positive displacement compressor datasheet

diesel-generator.standard: IEC 60617 (generator) / layout and P&ID convention for the engine
diesel-generator.drawn: Rectangle for the diesel engine (marked D or DE) coupled to a circle with G and ~ for the alternator. On P&IDs it appears with its diesel (DF) supply line from a day tank and an exhaust line.
diesel-generator.notes: G with a turbine trapezoid is a gas-turbine-generator. DE coupled to a pump is a diesel-firewater-pump.

gas-turbine-compressor.drawn: A gas turbine (narrowing trapezoid, combustor box with the fuel line, widening trapezoid) coupled by its shaft to a compressor trapezoid, wide end at suction; anti-surge recycle and blowdown lines around the compressor.
gas-turbine-compressor.notes: A compressor coupled to a motor circle with M is the motor-driven version (centrifugal-compressor). A turbine coupled to a G circle is a gas-turbine-generator.

datasheet.form: API 616 gas turbine + API 617 compressor datasheets

vertical-turbine-pump.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (vertical / caisson pump convention)
vertical-turbine-pump.drawn: Pump set drawn vertically: motor (circle with M) on top, discharge head with a side outlet at deck level, and a long column hanging down into a caisson or sump with the pump bowls at the bottom, often below a sea-level mark.
vertical-turbine-pump.notes: Seawater lift and firewater pumps on offshore platforms are this type. A diesel driver box instead of M means diesel-firewater-pump. Some legends draw only a pump circle with "VS1" or "caisson" written beside it.

diesel-firewater-pump.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001; NFPA 20 fire pump
diesel-firewater-pump.drawn: Pump symbol (or vertical caisson pump) coupled to a rectangle marked D, DE or "diesel" for the engine driver, on a firewater (FW) line feeding the ring main, often inside a dashed pump-house boundary.
diesel-firewater-pump.notes: Same pump circle as any centrifugal pump: the diesel driver box, the FW line service and the firewater pump title decide it. An electric firewater (jockey) pump has M instead of DE.

datasheet.form: Fire pump datasheet (NFPA 20, API 610 VS1 / BB1)

between-bearings-pump.drawn: Same centrifugal pump circle (tangential discharge, side suction), here with the driver drawn as a circle with M on the shaft. High-head water injection or export duty, often noted "multistage" or "BB3".
between-bearings-pump.notes: The symbol does not show between-bearings or multistage construction; pick this component when the title, datasheet or duty says multistage / BB3 / high head (e.g. water injection, pipeline booster). Otherwise use centrifugal-pump.

vertical-inline-pump.drawn: Pump circle with suction and discharge on the same straight centreline through the casing (in-line), and the motor drawn above it on a vertical shaft.
vertical-inline-pump.notes: Many legends draw it as the normal centrifugal pump circle; the in-line nozzles and vertical motor are the clue when shown. Confirm OH3 / "vertical in-line" on the datasheet.

reciprocating-pump.drawn: Pump circle with a piston (a short thick bar) and rod inside, the rod leaving to a crank; suction in at the bottom and discharge out at the top, often with pulsation dampeners drawn as small domes on both lines.
reciprocating-pump.notes: A piston, plunger or crank inside the circle marks positive displacement. An adjustable-stroke arrow through it means a metering pump. Legends vary: some use a rectangle with a piston instead of a circle.

metering-pump.drawn: Small pump circle with a curved diaphragm line inside and a diagonal arrow through it (adjustable capacity), on a chemical injection (CI) line, usually inside a chemical injection package boundary.
metering-pump.notes: The diagonal arrow (variable stroke) and the small CI / MI line size tell it from a centrifugal pump. Several identical heads in a row inside a dashed box = a chemical-injection-skid.

electric-motor.drawn: Circle with M (IEC: M with 3~ underneath for a three-phase AC motor), drawn coupled to the driven machine on P&IDs and hanging from a feeder on single-line diagrams.
electric-motor.notes: Circle with G is a generator. A circle with M on top of a valve stem is a motor actuator (MOV), not a separate motor. A circle with M inside a square is used by some legends for a motor-driven package.

centrifugal-fan.drawn: Circle (scroll) with a wide rectangular outlet duct leaving tangentially and curved blades or a hub drawn inside; inlet through the centre. Axial fans are drawn as a propeller (bow-tie) inside a circle or duct.
centrifugal-fan.notes: Looks like a pump but the outlet is a wide duct and it sits on HVAC ducting (often drawn double-line) rather than a pipe. Air cooler fans are part of air-cooled-exchanger.

progressive-cavity-pump.drawn: Rotary pump outline (a long rounded casing or circle) with a helical rotor drawn as a wavy line inside, suction into the top of the suction housing and discharge out of the end; driver on the shaft.
progressive-cavity-pump.notes: Many legends use the general rotary PD pump symbol with "PC" or "progressive cavity" beside it. Used for viscous, sandy or shear-sensitive liquids (drains, sludge, crude transfer).

submersible-pump.standard: ISO 10628-2 / PIP PIC001 (caisson / submersible pump convention)
submersible-pump.drawn: A pump hanging in a caisson below sea level with the motor (circle with M) BELOW the pump bowls at the bottom of the string, the discharge riser going up to the top plate and a power cable alongside.
submersible-pump.notes: Motor at the bottom = submersible; motor on top of the deck = vertical-turbine-pump (line shaft). Some legends draw only a pump circle in the caisson with "ESP" or "submersible" written.

centrifugal-pump.drawn: Circle with the discharge leaving tangentially from the top, suction entering the centre from the side. Often a small triangle inside pointing to the discharge, and a base line or two short legs under it.
centrifugal-pump.notes: P&IDs rarely show the API 610 type. OH2, OH3, BB3 and VS pumps can all appear as this circle: read the datasheet or the title (e.g. "multistage", "vertical inline", "caisson"). A circle with a piston or crank inside is a reciprocating pump; an arrow through the symbol means variable capacity (metering pump).

toxic-gas-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); ISA 5.1 AT tag
toxic-gas-detector.drawn: F&G layout: a gas-detector symbol (circle, sometimes a triangle) with T, TOX or the gas (H2S, CO, SO2) and the ppm set points written beside it; on C&E charts an AT bubble.
toxic-gas-detector.notes: Same family as point-gas-detector: the gas name decides. Flammable detectors read % LEL; toxic detectors read ppm.

acoustic-gas-leak-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); ISA TR84.00.07 mapping practice
acoustic-gas-leak-detector.drawn: F&G layout: a detector symbol marked U, UGLD or AGLD with its detection radius (a dashed circle, typically 5–20 m) drawn around it; sound-wave arcs on some legends.
acoustic-gas-leak-detector.notes: Large coverage circles centred on a detector are ultrasonic (acoustic); flame detectors show a cone; open-path detectors a beam line.

hydrogen-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company)
hydrogen-detector.drawn: F&G or HVAC layout: a gas-detector symbol with H2 written beside it, placed at the ceiling high point of battery rooms, UPS rooms and electrolyser enclosures; on C&E charts an AT bubble with the % LEL set points.
hydrogen-detector.notes: Hydrogen detectors sit at ceiling level (H2 is lighter than air); hydrocarbon point detectors in process areas are usually lower.

datasheet.form: Gas detector datasheet (IEC 60079-29-1; IEC 62485-2 battery rooms)

aspirating-smoke-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); EN 54-20
aspirating-smoke-detector.drawn: A detector box marked ASD (or VESDA) with a sampling pipe running across the ceiling plan and the sampling holes marked as dots or short ticks along it.
aspirating-smoke-detector.notes: A pipe line with sampling holes from a box = aspirating system; point smoke detectors are individual circles with S.

beam-smoke-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); EN 54-12
beam-smoke-detector.drawn: A transceiver symbol at one end and a reflector (square with a cross) at the other, joined by a beam line (often double-headed or a pair of lines) across a large open space.
beam-smoke-detector.notes: Reflector at one end (no receiver electronics) = reflective beam smoke detector. A transmitter / receiver pair with a single beam on a process area is an open-path gas detector.

pa-loudspeaker.drawn: IEC loudspeaker: a small rectangle with a flared trumpet (trapezoid) opening from it, drawn at each speaker position on the PA/GA layout with its power tap (e.g. 15 W) and aiming direction.
pa-loudspeaker.notes: An alarm sounder is drawn as a bell or horn; a combined beacon and sounder is alarm-beacon. PA loudspeakers carry a wattage note.

emergency-light.drawn: Lighting layout: the luminaire outline (a long rectangle for a linear fitting, a circle for a bulkhead) with a filled mark, a cross or E for the emergency / self-contained battery version and the duration (e.g. 3 h) beside it.
emergency-light.notes: The filled mark or E distinguishes emergency fittings from normal luminaires on the same drawing. Escape signs are drawn separately (escape-sign).

escape-sign.standard: ISO 7010 / ISO 3864-1 (safety signs), escape plan convention
escape-sign.drawn: On escape route plans: a small sign rectangle showing the ISO 7010 emergency exit or assembly point symbol with a direction arrow, at each change of direction along the escape route; route arrows drawn along the walkways.
escape-sign.notes: Only on escape and safety plans. Muster / assembly points use the square E007-type sign; exits use the rectangular sign with an arrow.

emergency-telephone.drawn: Telecom or escape layout: a telephone symbol (box with a handset) at the phone position, labelled EMERGENCY or with its extension; booths and acoustic hoods noted.
emergency-telephone.notes: Only on telecom and escape layouts. A box with only a push-button is a manual call point.

fire-hydrant.standard: F&G / safety layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); NFPA 24 / EN 14384
fire-hydrant.drawn: Fire-protection layouts: a hydrant symbol (a circle with outlet stubs, or a pillar with two side outlets) on the underground firewater main, tagged H or FH; on the firewater P&ID a branch off the ring with an isolation valve.
fire-hydrant.notes: A riser with a nozzle barrel is a fire monitor; a reel is a hose reel. Pillar hydrants are onshore; offshore uses hose stations and monitors on the ring main.

deluge-nozzle.drawn: On deluge layouts and isometrics: a short drop from the deluge pipe ending in a nozzle (small open cone or triangle) with its spray pattern; closed sprinkler heads are a circle with a dot. The nozzle type and K-factor are tabulated.
deluge-nozzle.notes: Open nozzle (no bulb) = deluge; a sprinkler head (bulb) is drawn as a filled circle or circle with a dot. On P&IDs a deluge network is one line after the deluge valve with "nozzles" noted.

breathing-apparatus-cabinet.standard: Safety equipment layout convention; ISO 7010 sign
breathing-apparatus-cabinet.drawn: Safety equipment layouts: a cabinet rectangle with a BA mark or a cylinder outline, located at muster points, the CCR and H2S-risk areas, with the number of sets noted.
breathing-apparatus-cabinet.notes: Only on safety equipment plans. A cabinet with a cross is a first-aid station; a cabinet with FE is an extinguisher.

datasheet.form: Safety equipment schedule (EN 137 / SOLAS FSS Code ch. 3)

first-aid-station.standard: Safety equipment layout convention; ISO 7010 sign
first-aid-station.drawn: Safety equipment layouts: a square with a cross (the first-aid sign) at the station, with a stretcher noted where provided.
first-aid-station.notes: Only on safety equipment plans. The cross outline tells it from other cabinets.

lifejacket-box.standard: Lifesaving appliance plan convention; SOLAS LSA Code, ISO 7010 sign
lifejacket-box.drawn: Escape and lifesaving plans: a box (rectangle) with a lifejacket outline or LJ mark at each muster station and lifeboat embarkation point, with the number of jackets stored written beside it.
lifejacket-box.notes: Only on lifesaving appliance plans. A ring is a lifebuoy (life-ring); a boat outline is a lifeboat.

fire-blanket.standard: Safety equipment layout convention; ISO 7010 sign
fire-blanket.drawn: Safety equipment layouts: a small rectangle marked FB (fire blanket) on the wall of galleys, workshops and laboratories, sometimes with the pull tabs drawn below.
fire-blanket.notes: Only on safety equipment plans. FE marks an extinguisher; HR a hose reel.

point-gas-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); ISA 5.1 AT / GD tag
point-gas-detector.drawn: On F&G layouts: a circle (or hexagon / triangle on some legends) with G, GD or the gas (HC, H2S, H2) inside or beside it, placed at the detector position with its tag. On cause & effect and some P&IDs it is an AT / GD bubble with the gas and LEL set points written beside it.
point-gas-detector.notes: Point detectors are single symbols; open-path detectors are a pair joined by a beam line. Toxic (H2S, CO) detectors use the same symbol with the gas name; a separate toxic-gas-detector component covers electrochemical cells.

flame-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); cone of vision per NORSOK Z-001 / ISA TR84.00.07 mapping practice
flame-detector.drawn: A detector symbol (circle with F or FD, or a small triangle) with a wedge or cone drawn from it showing the field of view, aimed into the area it covers; the tilt angle is often written beside it.
flame-detector.notes: The cone of vision is the giveaway. A pair of symbols joined by a beam line is an open-path gas detector. ISA uses B (burner / combustion) for flame: BE / BT / BSH on some P&IDs.

open-path-gas-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); IEC 60079-29-4
open-path-gas-detector.drawn: Two symbols, a transmitter and a receiver, at the two ends of a straight dashed beam line across the area, often labelled OGD with the path length and LEL·m set points.
open-path-gas-detector.notes: The beam line between a pair of symbols is the clue; a single symbol with a cone is a flame detector. Some legends draw an arrow from transmitter to receiver.

manual-call-point.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); EN 54-11, ISO 7010 sign
manual-call-point.drawn: A square with a filled circle (or a small square) in the middle, at the call point position on escape routes and exits, labelled MAC / MCP; ESD push-buttons use the same box marked ESD or with a different fill.
manual-call-point.notes: NFPA-style US legends draw the pull station as a square with F or a hand. On P&IDs and C&E charts a manual call point is an HS bubble feeding the F&G logic.

alarm-beacon.standard: IEC 60617 (lamp, horn) / F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company)
alarm-beacon.drawn: On F&G and PA/GA layouts: a lamp symbol (circle with ×) with short light rays for the beacon, and a horn outline (trumpet) for the sounder, labelled with the colour and the GA / F&G status it shows.
alarm-beacon.notes: Circle with × alone is a general lamp (lighting); the rays and colour note mark a status beacon. Sounders alone are a horn outline or a bell.

datasheet.form: Visual / audible alarm device datasheet (EN 54-23 / EN 54-3)

deluge-valve-skid.standard: ISO 10628-2 valves + NFPA 15 / NFPA 170 deluge convention
deluge-valve-skid.drawn: On the firewater P&ID: a deluge valve (valve body with a solenoid release box, tagged DV / XV) between two locked-open (LO) isolation valves, feeding a dry deluge pipe network drawn to the nozzles; often inside a dashed skid boundary.
deluge-valve-skid.notes: Look for the firewater (FW) line, the LO marks and the dry pipe downstream. A plain ESDV on a process line is esd-valve. Some legends draw the deluge valve as a check-valve body with a clapper. ISA codes here: XY = solenoid; PSL = trip.

fire-monitor.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); NFPA 170-style fire protection symbol
fire-monitor.drawn: On fire-protection layouts: a riser with a swivel (small circle) and a tapered nozzle barrel, sometimes with an arc showing the throw or the oscillation sector; on the firewater P&ID it is a branch off the ring main with an LO isolation valve and FM / MON tag.
fire-monitor.notes: A hose reel shows a drum with coiled hose; a hydrant is a riser with outlets and no barrel. Foam monitors are the same symbol with a foam (AFFF) supply.

hose-reel.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company)
hose-reel.drawn: Circle with a smaller concentric circle (the drum) and the hose leaving to a nozzle, labelled HR; on the firewater P&ID a small branch off the ring main with a ball valve and HR tag.
hose-reel.notes: Concentric circles = reel. A riser with a nozzle barrel is a fire monitor; a box with letters FE or a cylinder outline is an extinguisher.

safety-shower.standard: Layout plan convention; ISO 7010 sign; ANSI Z358.1
safety-shower.drawn: On layouts: a shower head (dome) on a pipe with spray lines and an eyewash bowl, or a box marked SS / EW with the ISO 7010 green sign; on utility P&IDs a small potable-water branch ending in an SS tag.
safety-shower.notes: Placed near chemical injection, battery rooms and laboratories. A box marked EW alone is a standalone eyewash.

datasheet.form: Emergency shower and eyewash datasheet (ANSI Z358.1 / EN 15154)

fire-extinguisher.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company); ISO 7010 safety sign
fire-extinguisher.drawn: On fire-protection layouts: a small extinguisher outline or a triangle / square with the agent letters (DP, CO2, FOAM) and size (e.g. 9 kg); wheeled units are marked W or with wheels.
fire-extinguisher.notes: Legends vary a lot; read the letters for the agent and capacity. Not shown on P&IDs.

windsock.standard: Layout plan convention; CAP 437 / ICAO Annex 14 helideck marking
windsock.drawn: On helideck and platform layouts: a mast with a truncated cone (the sock) streaming from it, sometimes only a small circle at the mast position labelled WS.
windsock.notes: Located clear of the helideck obstacle-free sector, visible from the approach. Not shown on P&IDs.

datasheet.form: Helideck windsock specification (CAP 437 / ICAO Annex 14 Vol II)

heat-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company)
heat-detector.drawn: Circle (or square on NFPA-style legends) with H or HD, placed on the ceiling plan of enclosed modules or near specific equipment (turbine hoods, battery rooms); fixed-temperature or rate-of-rise noted beside it.
heat-detector.notes: Letters inside the circle distinguish detector types: H heat, S smoke, F flame, G gas. On some P&IDs heat detection is a TSH bubble or a fusible-plug loop on the instrument air.

smoke-detector.standard: F&G layout convention (NFPA 170 / ISO 7240-style plan symbols; legends vary by company)
smoke-detector.drawn: Circle (or square) with S or SD on the ceiling plan of enclosed rooms: LER, CCR, accommodation and HVAC ducts (duct detectors marked D).
smoke-detector.notes: Same family as the heat detector: read the letter. BS-style legends draw a smoke detector as a circle with S; NFPA-style may use a square or SD in a circle.

life-ring.standard: Layout plan convention (lifesaving appliance plan); SOLAS LSA Code, ISO 7010 sign
life-ring.drawn: On escape and lifesaving appliance plans: a ring (two concentric circles) with four bands, at each lifebuoy station; a light or smoke signal is marked L / S beside it.
life-ring.notes: Only on escape / lifesaving plans, never on P&IDs.

deck-module.standard: Layout plan convention (structural / plot plan drawings); ISO 19902
deck-module.drawn: Plan view: the deck outline with dash-dot structural grid lines (rows and columns, e.g. A–D and 1–6) and circles at the jacket leg positions; deck elevations (EL +28.000 TOS) written in the corners.
deck-module.notes: Not on P&IDs. Equipment layouts use this outline as the background; the grid labels locate equipment. A smaller framed rectangle with bracing is a module-frame.

datasheet.form: Structural design basis / deck framing drawing (ISO 19902, NORSOK N-004)

pipe-rack.standard: Layout plan convention (structural / plot plan drawings) (rack cross-section)
pipe-rack.drawn: Cross-section: a portal frame (two posts and one or more tier beams) with the pipes drawn as circles resting on each tier; in plan, two parallel lines with the bent positions marked across them and the pipes as lines along the rack.
pipe-rack.notes: Not on P&IDs (lines there are schematic). Cable trays on the top tier appear as narrow rectangles. A single post with arms is a cable-tray support.

stair.standard: Layout plan convention (structural / plot plan drawings); ISO 14122-3
stair.drawn: Plan view: a rectangle filled with parallel tread lines and an arrow along it labelled UP (or DN), often with a break line half-way.
stair.notes: Rungs at close spacing with a circle around them is a caged ladder seen in plan. Not on P&IDs.

ladder.standard: Layout plan convention (structural / plot plan drawings); ISO 14122-4
ladder.drawn: Elevation: two stiles with rungs and hoops of the safety cage; in plan, a short pair of lines with a semicircle (the cage) against the platform edge, labelled LADDER.
ladder.notes: A stair has an inclined flight with an UP arrow; a ladder is vertical. Not on P&IDs.
